open: [STUB] Ring Two's food stalls hum while a loader argues with a scanner two rows over. The stallholder slaps her receipt down. She says forty paid bowls were never collected. The crew lead holds up a matching receipt and says the order went out and was paid for twice. Unless someone rules before the bell, the crew boycotts and the Exchange clerk logs a complaint.

clean.text: [STUB] Onions fry somewhere above while half the price of forty bowls is laid on the counter. The stallholder counts it on her fingers, nods, and tears her receipt across the middle. The crew lead nods once. By the bell, diners down the row are repeating the crew's name as the ones who settled it.

cost.text: [STUB] Warm bowls are stacked for the crew, and the stallholder demands her half in coin before she will lower her voice. A thousand credits slide across the counter and vanish into her apron. She tears the stall's receipt in two. The crew lead keeps hers and mutters that no order was worth that much.

fail.text: [STUB] The stallholder snaps a lid onto a bowl and says she will not pay for what she never lost. The crew lead says the same about what was paid. Voices climb until a neighbouring cook bangs a ladle on a pot. Both sides agree to bring their receipts to the Exchange desk at tomorrow's first shift, and the crew walks off with tension pulled tight across their shoulders.

clean.text: [STUB] The scale's brass pan reads true, and the stallholder's book shows one entry for forty bowls beside a smudged stamp. The crew's receipt carries the same stamp, printed twice by a jammed register. The stallholder exhales, closes the book, and pushes the crew's coin back across the counter. Shoulders loosen all down the row.

cost.text: [STUB] Covered bowls of beans from the stall by the water reclaimer sit ignored while the receipts are checked line by line. The stallholder's double entry turns up, and she hands five hundred credits across for the overcharge. Counting every line takes the whole hour, and a dull ache settles behind the temples of everyone leaning over the books.

fail.text: [STUB] The scale tips and the pages blur, and a fumbled catch on the tally drawer snaps its hinge. The stallholder wants the repair paid on the spot, and five hundred credits go into her palm. The receipts settle nothing today. Take both to the registry desk the morning after next, where the stamp roll can be matched.

clean.text: [STUB] The Exchange clerk arrives, runs a thumb along both receipts, and finds the same order number stamped twice. She writes the ruling on the spot: the stall pays the crew one thousand credits for the second charge. The stallholder glares at the clerk but signs. The bell finds the dispute closed.

cost.text: [STUB] The clerk's ruling comes with a filing charge of five hundred credits from the crew, written in blue ink on the docket. The order is split down the middle, and each side keeps its own receipt. Chairs scrape as the crowd drifts back to its meals. The stallholder will not look at the crew.

fail.text: [STUB] The clerk reads both receipts through twice, frowns at the clock, and hands the stallholder a slip for the window at second shift. Her sleeve is already past the stall corner. The crew lead mutters that the clerk could have ruled in a minute, and the shouting that follows leaves everyone sore. The bell rings over a slip and an empty chair.

ending: [STUB] The walkway of Ring Two carries on in its usual din. The ledger card follows.
